The draft's quoted phrase is verbatim from the source and the connective framing ('per the House Rules and Manual, that change was made ...') adds no new claim beyond what the source itself states. The source phrase is genuinely ambiguous between two readings (the amendment restored M/T/W without also restoring the historic end-of-session expansion; vs. the M/T/W restoration carves out the last six days) — but that ambiguity is inherent to the source's own phrasing, not draft-added distortion. Rewriting to disambiguate would require importing historical interpretation the source does not directly state. Draft renders the source faithfully and adds no editorial gloss.
